## Design Brief
Clear description of what needs to be designed and its strategic importance for the rebranding initiative.

## Strategic Context
- **Brand Objective**: How this design supports the AI platform transformation
- **User Experience**: Impact on individual developers and enterprise users
- **Competitive Advantage**: How this design element differentiates us

## Design Requirements

### Functional Requirements
- **Core Function**: What this design must accomplish
- **User Interactions**: How users will interact with this design
- **Technical Constraints**: Platform/format limitations
- **Performance Needs**: Loading speed, responsiveness, etc.

### Brand Requirements
- **Brand Personality**: How this should feel (intelligent, approachable, reliable)
- **Visual Style**: Alignment with emerging brand direction
- **Tone Expression**: How brand personality shows in this design
- **Consistency**: How this fits with other brand elements

### Technical Requirements
- **Platforms**: Where this will be used (web, CLI, mobile, print)
- **Formats**: File types and specifications needed
- **Scalability**: Size variations and responsive needs
- **Integration**: How this works with existing systems

### Accessibility Requirements
- **WCAG Compliance**: Level AA compliance required
- **Color Contrast**: Minimum contrast ratios
- **Screen Readers**: Alt text and semantic requirements
- **Keyboard Navigation**: If applicable

## Target Audience

### Primary Audience
- **Demographics**: Individual Go developers (2-15 years experience)
- **Behavior**: How they currently use go-starter
- **Pain Points**: What frustrates them about current experience
- **Goals**: What they want to accomplish

### Secondary Audience
- **Demographics**: Enterprise development teams and decision makers
- **Behavior**: How they evaluate and adopt development tools
- **Pain Points**: Governance, standardization, scale challenges
- **Goals**: Team efficiency, consistency, compliance

### Use Cases
1. **Key Scenario 1**: Specific context where this design will be used
2. **Key Scenario 2**: Secondary use case that must be supported
3. **Edge Cases**: Unusual but important scenarios to consider

## Design Process

### Discovery Phase
- [ ] Audit existing design elements
- [ ] Analyze competitor approaches
- [ ] Review user research insights
- [ ] Define design principles

### Concept Phase
- [ ] Generate 3-5 distinct design directions
- [ ] Create low-fidelity concepts
- [ ] Internal design review
- [ ] Stakeholder feedback session

### Development Phase
- [ ] Refine chosen concept(s)
- [ ] Create high-fidelity designs
- [ ] Develop variations and applications
- [ ] Design system integration

### Validation Phase
- [ ] User testing (if applicable)
- [ ] Accessibility review
- [ ] Technical feasibility check
- [ ] Stakeholder approval

## Deliverables
- [ ] Concept explorations (3-5 design directions)
- [ ] Design rationale document
- [ ] Final design files (source formats)
- [ ] Production assets (web/print ready)
- [ ] Usage guidelines and specifications
- [ ] Design system integration documentation

## Timeline
- **Discovery & Research**: Week X
- **Concept Development**: Week Y
- **Refinement & Development**: Week Z
- **Testing & Validation**: Week Z+1
- **Final Assets & Documentation**: Week Z+2

## Budget
- **Design Tools/Software**: $XXX
- **Stock Photography/Icons**: $XXX
- **User Testing**: $XXX
- **External Design Vendor**: $XXX
- **Total Estimated Cost**: $XXX

## Review Process

### Internal Review
- [ ] Design team peer review
- [ ] Creative director review
- [ ] Brand consistency check
- [ ] Technical feasibility review

### Stakeholder Review
- [ ] Marketing team approval
- [ ] Engineering team technical review
- [ ] Executive stakeholder sign-off
- [ ] Legal/compliance review (if applicable)

### User Validation
- [ ] User testing sessions (if applicable)
- [ ] A/B testing setup (if applicable)
- [ ] Feedback incorporation
- [ ] Final validation

## Quality Standards
- **Visual Quality**: Professional, polished appearance
- **Brand Consistency**: Aligns with brand guidelines
- **Usability**: Intuitive and user-friendly
- **Accessibility**: Meets WCAG AA standards
- **Technical Quality**: Production-ready files

## File Organization
- **Source Files**: Working files in native formats
- **Production Assets**: Optimized files for implementation
- **Archive**: Versioned storage of all iterations
- **Documentation**: Usage guides and specifications

## Success Metrics
- [ ] Stakeholder approval received (specify approvers)
- [ ] User testing validation (if applicable)
- [ ] Technical implementation successful
- [ ] Brand consistency maintained
- [ ] Accessibility standards met
- [ ] Timeline and budget met

## Risk Management
**High Risk:**
- Concept rejection → Multiple directions, early feedback
- Technical constraints → Early engineering consultation
- Accessibility issues → Built-in accessibility review

**Medium Risk:**
- Timeline delays → Buffer time, parallel workstreams
- Stakeholder alignment → Regular check-ins, clear criteria

## Dependencies
- [ ] Brand personality definition completed
- [ ] Color palette and typography established
- [ ] Related design elements completed
- [ ] User research insights available

## Related Work
- **Depends On**: Other design issues that must be completed first
- **Informs**: Design work that will build on this
- **Integrates With**: Concurrent design work that must align

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All functional requirements met
- [ ] Brand requirements satisfied
- [ ] Technical specifications achieved
- [ ] Accessibility standards met
- [ ] All deliverables completed to quality standards
- [ ] Stakeholder approval received
- [ ] Implementation documentation complete
- [ ] Files organized and archived properly

## Implementation Support
- **Engineering Handoff**: How design will be transferred to development
- **Quality Assurance**: How implementation will be validated
- **Launch Support**: Designer availability during implementation
- **Iteration Plan**: How design will be refined post-launch
